body:
SCOUT fresh-context read-only review of corrected P0-2 candidate c9a2b7f (no edits). Three pre-ack findings, all against the committed tree:

1. REQUIRED — AttemptReceipt identity does not commit to all of its value. contract.scala:120-139 includes embeddingReceipts in equality, but rendering/of at 210-269 omits embeddingReceipts entirely and does not require providerCalls == embeddingReceipts.map(_.call) or receipt.isKeyConsistent. Because AttemptReceipt.of is public, callers can vary embeddingReceipts independently while preserving the same digest. Fix by deriving calls from validated embedding receipts or rendering/validating the nested receipts; pin a same-digest/different-embeddingReceipts adversarial law.

2. REQUIRED — Withheld can still describe provider calls. EmbeddingReceipt Scaladoc says Withheld never describes a provider call (receipt.scala:196-201), but AttemptReceipt.failClosed accepts and preserves providerCalls/embeddingReceipts (contract.scala:329-359); addResultDecisions uses that path with existing calls at 182-205, and cache fallback passes fresh calls at cache.scala:165-173. Make failClosed incapable of carrying calls/embedding receipts, or return Either/refuse nonempty provenance. Pin providerCalls.isEmpty && embeddingReceipts.isEmpty for every Withheld receipt.

3. REQUIRED ownership law — the once-key snapshot still aliases mutable input. cache.scala:85-87 passes keys.key(...) bytes into SensitiveKeyProvider.static; static captures that Array and clones only on later reads (digest.scala:84-89). A provider returning an aliased array can mutate it after CacheKey minting but before AttemptReceipt minting, so the claimed batch snapshot changes. Clone on capture (or use an immutable secret-byte owner) and test a provider whose underlying embed mutates the returned array mid-batch.

Verified from source at c9a2b7f; I did not rerun the already-posted platform gate because these are constructor/ownership defects not exercised by the 82 laws. Chief decides severity/disposition.
